# CTH-LIT-13 author research (evaluator-only; never runner evidence)

This is a simulated first-pass review under supplied Cascade protocols, not a current-law opinion or a served privilege log. The reference skill informs workflow and cautious triage only. Original evidence and native text were inspected; no demo privilege log or hidden label supplies any conclusion. Source hashes and exact extracted body-line/page/sheet locators are in research_sources.json. Native PDF text was complete for the six engagement PDFs reviewed; neither OCR nor image interpretation was needed for these selected sources. PNG signatures/logos are not substantive review targets. The broader evidence bundle records other extraction limitations.

Cutoff proposed: 2023-12-31T23:59:59-08:00. Dates are source dates, distinct from later compilation time. The DOCX protocols are supplied evaluation rules prepared in 2026, not historical 2023 communications. Original protocol worked examples explicitly mention answer IDs; public input must use the rule-only projection, excluding case-answer examples. Candidate findings below independently use original matter documents.

## Seven findings and meaningful contrasts

1. **GC advice before the supplied work-product trigger.** EMAIL-012 dated October 4, 2022, From Ellery to Marlowe, body line 3: “this memo and my analysis ... are provided as legal advice”; recommendation pauses placements pending eligibility and licensing clearance. Attachment Privileged_Coastal_Solar_Risk_Assessment.pdf p1 identifies Ellery, October 4, 2022, and analyzes exposure/recommends a pause. ACP supported; WP unsupported under supplied February 24, 2023 trigger despite attachment's work-product banner. Equivalent substantive proof: attachment sections I/IV/V, not merely privilege heading. Counterevidence is actual pre-trigger date. Labels cannot override chronology.

2. **Outside-counsel cover and retention attachment are different items.** EMAIL-021 February 24, 2023, body line3 “Formally engaging L&L Associates to advise on the internal review ... given the complaint received last week” supports a legal-services request. LL_Associates_Engagement_Letter.pdf p1: “This letter confirms the engagement ... to provide legal advice and conduct an internal review”. The attachment is the retention record, independently administrative; its privilege/work-product banner does not make every family member privileged. The task may grade ACP family distinction but should leave WP of the cover cautiously ungraded/attorney-review rather than inventing strategy in a retention message.

3. **Whitaker's counsel-directed analysis versus an unchanged client template.** EMAIL-529 dated September10, from Whitaker to Lin, body line1: “as you asked, I've started tracing the fee wires”, “Prepared at your direction”, and describes fee tracing; support needs the engagement join. EMAIL-137 body line3 and actual Kovel_Engagement_Whitaker_Forensic.pdf p1 establish retained by L&L, solely its direction, assisting legal advice for anticipated litigation, no direct audit/tax services to CTH. EMAIL-138 body line1 confirms reporting only to L&L; EMAIL-141 body line3 is alternate corroboration. ACP and fact-WP candidate for EMAIL-529, subject to first-pass review; no opinion-WP finding required. Attached booking_note.csv contains only header batch,face_value,cash_received,fees_expensed and row NW-batch,,,; EMAIL-529 says “the columns are blank, which is how it came to us”. The preexisting template does not inherit email protection. Do not classify all accountant records alike.

4. **Larsen ordinary-course purpose persists through a bare forward to counsel.** EMAIL-145 From Craig to Ellery August22 top line “FYI —”, no advice request. Quoted original line19 discusses final provision memo, deferred revenue, contingency disclosure; line35 requests “usual provision support” and “Same scope as last year”. Earlier Larsen Q3/Q4 2022 and Q1 2023 engagement PDFs p1 confirm standard business engagement “not at counsel direction”; contemporaneous EMAIL-143/144 may be acceptable equivalents after direct verification. No blanket Kovel inference from tax subject, examination mention, legal recipient, or subsequent date. The purported provision memo is not actually attached to EMAIL-145, so no claim that its page3 was inspected is permissible.

5. **Third-party placement forward is business correspondence.** EMAIL-151 From Priya Shah at Alder to Ellery; top body signature only, then Renee Ford/Bellhaven asks at line11 “any word on when placements might resume?” and mentions interested buyers. Outsider role plus operational purpose rebuts legal-recipient shortcut. ACP not supported; WP not supported on this record. It is not a legal advice disclosure merely because counsel receives it. Distinguish original Renee-to-Priya communication and Priya's bare forward.

6. **Mixed financial model needs an explicit unresolved-purpose flag.** EMAIL-071 July10 from controller Sato to CFO Denniston, no counsel participant, line1 Q3 pause impact plus L&L review costs before board session. Q3_Financial_Impact_Coastal_Solar_Pause.xlsx sheet Q3 Impact A1:D5 has revenue, broker fees, review costs and net effect. It contains no counsel direction, but no comprehensive inquiry settles whether it was prepared because of litigation. Under supplied uncertain-purpose rule: ACP unsupported for email/model, WP needs attorney review; preserve candidate designation and seek instruction/provenance. Costs for L&L alone do not establish WP. EMAIL-1473 describes a *different* restricted exposure workbook; never transfer counsel direction across files based only on finance subject similarity.

7. **Auditor waiver risk is not proof of actual disclosure.** EMAIL-1472 June7 line1 requests advice about Brenda's Q2 support inquiry and asks “What am I allowed to give her?” EMAIL-1473 internal To/CC includes client personnel and Lin, line3 “Don't send Moss & Lane the workbook or anything from this chain”; line5 limits response to ordinary close support, management has not adopted estimate. Original EX_Moss_Audit_Engagement_FY2022.pdf p1 establishes financial-statement audit/testing, not legal-agent retainer. The internal legal communication supports ACP/opinion-WP candidate; assess sharing risk and retain attorney-review flag, but do not conclude the workbook was disclosed or protection waived. Later remediation-pilot packets sent to Moss are different items; disclose nothing from this simulated task.

## Protocol rule locators read directly from DOCX XML paragraphs

ACP: ¶26–36 confidentiality/persons/purpose and ordinary/admin exceptions; ¶38–49 roles and outsiders; ¶52–53 substance over labels (exclude misleading reliable-header assertion from public input); ¶61–64 engagement family distinction (case example excluded); ¶70–73 independent family and attorney participation; ¶76–81 counsel-retained agent test; ¶93–94 responsiveness independent.
WP: ¶24–27 because-of-litigation, fact/opinion distinction; ¶29–33 February24 trigger (exclude case examples); ¶47–48 sharing with IRS; ¶49–51 ambiguous purpose (exclude named case); ¶55–56 waiver. Caution: ¶54 GreenAcre shorthand conflicts with ¶33 pre-trigger treatment; don't use that shorthand as normative answer evidence.

## Equivalence and limits

Use document-level proposition groups and quoted factual support verified against retrieved source text. Accept alternate quotations within reviewed substantive source spans and duplicate original/quoted-thread proof when it actually includes the relevant proposition. Do not accept a title, banner, sender role or empty attachment as proof of legal purpose. There is no model entailment judge; deterministic proof checks approximate only the bounded reviewed propositions. Unreviewed equivalent proof must be surfaced for future oracle expansion, not represented as legal wrongness. Independent reviewer status remains pending until another agent checks these findings and adversarial tests.

PRIVILEGED AND CONFIDENTIAL — ATTORNEY-CLIENT COMMUNICATION / ATTORNEY WORK
 PRODUCT
MEMORANDUM
TO:  Elena Marlowe, Chief Executive Officer
FROM:  John Ellery, Head of Legal
DATE:  October 4, 2022
RE:  Coastal Solar Credit Program — Regulatory Exposure Assessment
I. Background
At your request, this memorandum summarizes the current regulatory exposure of the Coastal Solar
Credit Program based on our review to date. This analysis is provided as legal advice and is protected
by the attorney-client privilege and/or attorney work product doctrine.
II. Land Eligibility Documentation
Our review of conservation easement filings for a subset of parcels submitted with Coastal Solar credit
applications identified acreage figures that do not reconcile with the corresponding county filings. This
issue was first flagged internally by Alder Point personnel in March 2022 and has not, to our
knowledge, been resolved.
III. Broker Licensing Status
Bellhaven Advisory’s broker registration renewal in Oregon and Washington remains unresolved.
Bellhaven has represented that marketing in those states should pause until renewal clears; our
understanding is that marketing has continued.
IV. Regulatory Risk
Continued marketing and credit placement activity while these two issues remain open increases the
risk of regulatory scrutiny, including potential exposure under state broker licensing statutes and federal
tax credit eligibility rules.
V. Recommendation
We recommend pausing new Coastal Solar placements until (1) land eligibility documentation is
reconciled against county records, and (2) Bellhaven’s broker registration status in all active states is
confirmed current.

L&L ASSOCIATES
Outside Counsel - Attorneys at Law
July 27, 2023
VIA EMAIL
Dana Whitaker, CPA/CFF
Principal
Whitaker Forensic Accounting
Re: Engagement of Whitaker Forensic Accounting - Assistance to Counsel (Kovel)
Dear Ms. Whitaker:
This letter confirms the engagement of Whitaker Forensic Accounting ("you" or "the Firm") by L&L Associates ("we" or
"outside counsel") to assist us in rendering legal advice to our client, Cascade Timber Holdings, in connection with the
internal review of the Coastal Solar Credit Program and related litigation that we reasonably anticipate.
You will perform forensic accounting analysis of parcel payment records, credit sale proceeds, and related
disbursements identified by counsel. Your work will be performed solely at our direction and for the purpose of enabling
us to provide legal advice to our client; you will not provide accounting, audit, or tax services to Cascade Timber
Holdings directly.
All communications between you and this Firm, and all work papers, analyses, and deliverables prepared in connection
with this engagement, are confidential and are intended to be protected by the attorney-client privilege and the work
product doctrine, consistent with the principles of United States v. Kovel. You will deliver all work product exclusively to
this Firm, will mark all deliverables 'Privileged & Confidential - Prepared at the Direction of Counsel,' and will not
communicate regarding this engagement with any third party, including the client, without our prior instruction.
Fees will be billed to and paid by this Firm per the attached rate schedule. Please countersign and return this letter to
confirm.
Sincerely,
Grace Lin
Partner, L&L Associates
